evidence.quote: Today the Federal Open Market Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by ¼ percentage point, bringing it to ¾ to 1 percent.
We continue to expect that the ongoing strength of the economy will warrant gradual increases in the federal funds rate to achieve and maintain our objectives.
Today’s decision is in line with that view and does not represent a reassessment of the economic outlook or of the appropriate course for monetary policy.
we see the risks to the outlook as roughly balanced at this point
We’re not shooting for inflation above 2 percent, but it’s a reminder that there will be deviations above and below when we’re achieving our objective.
We made no decisions, and we will continue our discussion at subsequent meetings.

parsed.rationale: The Committee hiked 25bp and signaled further gradual increases toward neutral, citing solid labor-market progress. However, it emphasized that there was no change in outlook, balanced risks, a symmetric inflation goal and a low neutral rate, so the hawkish lean is moderate.
